title: Selling insurance for Atlanta Life by day, playing with Larkin by night
summary: After marrying in 1939 Cobb takes over his stepfather-in-law's insurance debit with Atlanta Life, working it while playing nights with Larkin.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Then I ended up with an automobile -- after I got married in 1939, writing writing insurance. How that came about, my stepfather-in-law, a man who was married to my wife's mother, had the biggest debit in the black insurance company here called Atlanta Life, whose home base is in Atlanta, Georgia.

He won -- he wrote more insurance for a trip to California, and he won the trip to California, and now if he wins a trip to California, who's gonna take care of the debit while he's gone? My wife's mother is a clerk at Atlanta Life. But he put me over -- he showed me how to draw the tick lines on the insurance, and every place he would go, he wrote a message out to me, you find this in the mailbox, you find this under the rug on the front porch, and he knew his route.

So he wrote all this out, and I had to go, and then what I couldn't make in a day as fast as he could, his wife knew, and when I picked her up at the office at 5 o'clock, she'd go with me to pick the rest of it up.
This is the truth. Then when he come back to me to make extra money, he got me in it and gave me $30 off his book and transferred it to me to get me started.

Now what I would do, I would work at night, playing music. I come home, my wife would go out in the morning until 12; she'd come back and she'd feed me and I'd take it in the afternoon and finish it up. That's the way we worked together.
Now, when you say you worked at night playing with the black music, was this with Milt Larkin's band?
